feature: 256-KiB HTTP/2 SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE for large single-stream messages

default_change.advertised_clamp: The SETTINGS value is min(max_frame_size, max_frame_payload), never below 16 KiB. This prevents advertising a frame the local allocation ceiling cannot receive.

candidate.design: Both netz endpoints advertise a 256-KiB SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE so a 256-KiB message can fit in one DATA frame and take the direct decoder path instead of cross-DATA reassembly.

benchmark_method.schedule: three ABBA rounds; default, candidate, candidate, default
benchmark_method.host: shared host with unrelated load; no CPU pinning
benchmark_method.metric: ns_per_roundtrip from the benchmark result record

small_message_control.conclusion: 0/512/4-KiB persistent and per-call workloads stayed within about 0.7% of the 16-KiB default.

full_suite_verification.webtransport_followup: The cancellation pacing wake test was made deterministic by lowering its pacing rate from 100000 to 1000 bytes/s so the cancellation wait reliably receives the DRAIN capsule. Library behavior was unchanged.

conclusion: A 256-KiB frame size makes a 256-KiB message fit one DATA frame and improves the persistent large-message workload by about 14.4% with no small-message regression. A 10-stream 1-MiB flow-control control was neutral-to-slightly faster, so the library now advertises 256 KiB by default; peers still start at the RFC 16-KiB value until SETTINGS exchange, and applications can explicitly select 16 KiB.
